**Finding submitted: deviation (INSURANCE), fallback target.**

The agreement does have an insurance clause — § 14 (p0048) — so this is not a genuinely absent clause. It provides:
- workers' compensation as required by statute ✓
- comprehensive general liability USD 1,000,000 ✓
- professional E&O USD 1,000,000 ✓ (meets the fallback element verbatim)
- certificates/evidence of insurance at Company's request ✓

**What fails:** no cyber/privacy coverage anywhere in the document, while Contractor handles our Confidential Information including "Company records and information" (§ 8, p0038) and may access Company computer systems and facilities (§ 1(c), p0007). That misses the fallback's cyber USD 2,000,000 element and sits close to walk-away territory for a vendor touching our data.

**Cure:** a single surgical replace inserting "and cyber and privacy liability insurance with coverage of at least two million dollars ($2,000,000)" into the existing coverage list, leaving the CGL, workers' compensation, certificates and notice mechanics untouched word-for-word. I did not upgrade to the preferred limits (CGL aggregate, E&O 2M, cyber 5M) — the fallback is the selected level and the E&O element was already met, so no operation restates it. Those preferred gaps are noted in the rationale only.
